summary: The Life at Conception Act declares that every human being from fertilization onward has a constitutional right to life under the 14th Amendment and requires equal protection of that right in all states and territories, while barring prosecution of any woman for the death of her unborn child.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures.
While abortion services are a component of healthcare, the bill does not address insurance coverage models, public programs, or market structures; its focus is solely on defining legal personhood.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration policy, borders, visas, or enforcement.

The bill explicitly declares that constitutional rights attach at fertilization and defines 'human person' to include the preborn from the moment of conception. This directly seeks to extend legal protections that would restrict or prohibit abortion access nationwide.
No provisions address military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
No provisions relate to environmental regulation, emissions, or conservation.
No provisions address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No provisions address schools, funding, curriculum, or education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill expressly disclaims any authorization to prosecute women and does not create new criminal penalties or sentencing rules.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No provisions address deficits, debt limits, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address sexual orientation, gender identity, or related legal protections.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting rights, election procedures, or voter qualifications.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions address employment, unions, wages, or worker protections.
The bill uses constitutional language rather than religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules; any connection is indirect at best.
